newsitem.title: FRANCE: Galliano locked into Cleopatra's grip.
newsitem.headline: Galliano locked into Cleopatra's grip.

text.p: Egyptian empresses in safety pins and pubescent school girls whose hormones are kicking in -- this is British designer John Galliano's fashion vision for next winter.
His show late on Thursday was a flurry of prep school uniforms turned racy, their grey flannel jackets squeezing nubile curves and pleated skirts clipped as high as the supermodel's underthings.

Then the pleated skirts became Egyptian loincloths and the models coiffed and made-up as Cleopatra, with snakeskin sandals that wound up the leg, and cobras staring mean from scaly golden head-dresses.
It was pure, pulsing theatre, from a tartan coat and bellbottoms swimming under a sea of brass buttons, to a heart- stopping liquid gold gown with gilt hands clasping the breasts.

There was Galliano's vintage romanticism when the models skulked out in sumptuous bias-cut chiffon with ruffles dribbling in spirals around the body, and his irreverent humour in a Union Jack toga or a frilly pink wisp over a transparent body stocking with a portrait of Jesus down the back.
Dresses of safety pins, visible nipples under sheer black catsuits, a turquoise snakeskin coat with a fur collar were all part of Galliano's mad vision
But oversexed Egyptian queens are no longer of this age and few are the women who can find an occasion, let alone the cash, to wear his otherworldly catwalk creations.
"Hollywood, parties, movie stars, the workmanship is fabulous. It's so inspiring," said Nicole Fischelis of U.S. departments store Saks Fifth Avenue. "He doesn't do this for ordinary people."

British actress and singer Jane Birkin, her arm around her actress daughter Charlotte Gainsbourg, described the clothes as "sexy". But asked if she would wear them, Birkin replied: "No, I'm not young enough."
Joseph Boitano of the exclusive department store Bergdorf Goodman said that under all of the theatrical paraphernalia, there were also down to earth clothes for today's woman.
"It's an amazing spectacle, very exciting and so much creativity. I'm certain that in the showroom , it will be put together in way that's wearable," he told Reuters.
"But the spirit is what's really important. John can come up with so many ideas, and it's amazingly executed," Boitano added.
Earlier, Lolita Lempicka stayed true to herself, spanning the fashion decades and the great designers

That meant a black silk gown whose neckline sloped beneath the breasts, leaving them bare, a magenta chiffon with roses and ruffles spilling down the off the shoulder neckline and a white antiquity-inspired gown creeping with golden ivy.
The rest was trendy and a sure sell: lace-edged slip dresses under masculine jackets, cardigans with Mongolian lamb collars and safety pin clasps on asymetric black jackets.
"I wanted to return to structured clothing, so I made a lot of masculine suits and jackets, and presented them with extremely feminine garments," Lempicka said after the show.

"I like to find inspiration in all different periods, from the beginning of the century to the 1930s. But in what I do there isn't really any epoch, except for little touches here and there, because I want to be modern in my own time," she said.
